The main mechanism is that each group element acts by a bijection and the measure is invariant under this transport.

- First show the basic identities
  \[
  \mu(c\!\cdot\!s)=\mu(s),\qquad
  (x\mapsto c\!\cdot\!x)^{-1}(s)=c^{-1}\!\cdot s.
  \]
  These immediately give both null-set preservation and the preimage-measure identity, so the first equivalence follows because both universally quantified statements hold.

- For the minimal-action assertion, prove that every nonempty open \(U\) has positive measure. Minimality makes the translates \(g\cdot U\) cover the whole space. If \(\mu(U)=0\), invariance makes every translate null. Regularity and \(\mu\ne0\) provide a compact set of positive measure; compactness reduces its cover by translates of \(U\) to finitely many null sets, a contradiction.

- Finally use
  \[
  c\cdot(s\cup c^{-1}\cdot t)=(c\cdot s)\cup t
  \]
  together with invariance to obtain the union-measure identity. Thus both sides of the second equivalence are again established independently.

The essential assumptions for the only nonformal step are minimality, regularity, and nonzeroness; they turn a nonempty open set into a positive-measure set.
